messages:
samira: FYI customer reported JSON-mode outputs containing literal \u escapes for Latin-1 chars when they set Content-Type: application/json; charset=Windows-1252. Repro below.

mike: rough impact?

samira: customer said schema validation fails downstream (strict-json) + some prompts get mis-parsed. It's hitting hosted API; they've attached a minimal repro.

samira: ```bash
# create payload with single é (0xE9) saved as windows-1252
printf "{\"text\": \"file: résumé\"}" > payload-win1252.json # save file in CP1252 encoding
curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=Windows-1252" --data-binary @payload-win1252.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete?structured_mode=json
```

elaine: what does response look like?

samira: response body (snip):

```json
{"id":"r1","choices":[{"text":"{\"name\": \"Jos\\u00e9\", \"note\": \"file: r\\u00e9sum\\u00e9\"}"}]}
```

samira: note that the inner JSON string contains literal backslash-u sequences (double-escaped) instead of the raw é. The customer expects unicode char, not escaped sequences, and their strict parser rejects it.

mike: hmm. RFC 8259 says JSON MUST be encoded in UTF-8, UTF-16, or UTF-32, but clients sometimes lie with charset headers. We should normalize. Is ingress honoring charset and re-encoding? @eng-infra-bot can you dump request bytes?

eng-infra-bot: trace_id=tr-9f3a; received Content-Type: application/json; charset=Windows-1252; raw-body-bytes=0x7b2264...e9...7d

elaine: looks like our parser currently decodes by applying header charset, then our output serializer escapes non-ASCII with \uXXXX. If the input was decoded from CP1252 to Unicode, we shouldn't double-escape when producing structured-mode strings.

mike: confirm: pipeline is [ingress decode -> model prompt builder -> structured serializer]. If ingress decodes using CP1252, characters become U+00E9, then serializer probably calls json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=True) which escapes non-ASCII to \u00e9. For structured_mode we want raw UTF-8 unicode in the inner string, not ascii-escaped.

samira: repro also shows streaming chunk boundaries sometimes split the escape sequences making parser errors: e.g. chunk 1 ends with "\\u00" and chunk 2 contains "e9" so client sees broken escape.

elaine: urgent because billing and parsing are regressions for this customer. Proposed mitigation: for structured_mode output, set ensure_ascii=False in serializer so unicode emits as UTF-8, and treat any charset param by transcoding to UTF-8 instead of leaving bytes. Also add chunk-safe escaping for streaming.

mike: agree. Patch idea: https://github.com/redwood-inc/inference/pull/12345 — add normalize_request_encoding() to ingress, always decode to unicode using header if valid, fallback to chardet detection, but then model input and serializer always operate on Unicode and serializer uses ensure_ascii=False for structured-mode.

samira: i've asked customer to test a quick workaround: force header to UTF-8 or reupload payload as UTF-8. They can also post-process server side to unescape, but we should fix server.

elaine: created incident INC-5532, linking trace tr-9f3a. @mike can you shepherd PR?

mike: yep, will open review today. :thumbsup:

samira: adding logs+examples to the incident doc. thanks all.
